final.public_statement:
Safety, quality, delivery and cost, always in that order. That's how we run this business, and it's how we made this call.

Here's what we know. CFM, with our partners at Safran, is on Airbus's new single-aisle, and we'll earn our place on it every day, on time on wing. We'll support that ramp on the signals Airbus gives us, jointly with Safran, and spares won't crowd out new engines. As the 737 MAX line steps down, we'll step down with it on Boeing's data, jointly with Safran. Inspection on safety-critical parts doesn't step down with the rate. LEAP-1A durability hardware is certified. It's in every new -1A engine and going into the fleet through the shops. We'll report LEAP time on wing in cycles once the fleet has proven it. The GEnx upgrade is ready for our 787 customers.

Here's what we don't know: when the next new narrowbodies will be launched, by whom, and on which engines. That's really not for us to say. It's the airframers' call. We don't have a birthright on that next order. We intend to earn it. A LEAP derivative is on offer to every airframer, and a new engine comes when an airframer and the returns are both there.

RISE stays all in as technology, together with Safran. When that architecture enters service is really not for us to say. We'll tell you about dates when the testing tells us.

We get paid in dollars, not in percentages. It's that simple, ain't that hard.
final.rationale:
DECISION: hold on ducted, open_fan, partner_embraer and lobby_emissions; genx can only be hold. Every field is at its default, so no item goes to the Board. Premium $0. No override.

1. WHAT GAME, HOW DO WE WIN [CX-0467, CX-0422]
It is the installed-base game, and on this board the window has nearly shut:
- The board counts the NB market to 2056 and the WB market to 2061.
- Anything launched today is ready in 2056 at the earliest. A Ducted counts one NB year (2056). Partner Embraer's share move counts from 2057. An Open Fan is ready in 2060.
- Slots: NGSA has had CFM fitted since 2037 alongside the rival engine, and every column carries that split. The fps and Embraer's jet are open, with no launch on the record. A LEAP derivative is on offer to both, and CFM is always available on a new airframe.
We win by running the LEAP fleet: time on wing, OE engines on time, spares that never crowd them out. RISE stays whole as joint technology. We are not going for share [CX-0493].

2. THE GRID AGAINST HOLD (S1 / S2 / S3, $B; check file /tmp/wargame-cfm/dash-2050-emb/work/r4_culp_decide.py, brief numbers only)
- Hold: -9.47 / -9.47 / -9.55. Best plan in every column. Weighted -9.48 at .65/.20/.15 and -9.50 at equal weights.
- Ducted: -5.78 / -5.78 / -5.78. It grosses $0.22B on a $6B bill ($4B R&D plus the $2B strain next to the running GEnx).
- Ducted + Partner Embraer: -5.78 / -5.78 / -5.58.
- Open Fan: -17.17 / -17.17 / -17.11, which is $7.1-7.2B beyond its $10B bill: the wait penalty, biting from 2050.
- Best Open Fan plan (Open Fan + Partner Embraer + Lobby): -15.10 / -15.10 / -14.86.
- Ducted + Open Fan combinations: -18.65 to -20.95.
Strain confirmed: the Ducted is worth +2.00 more next to an Open Fan than alone. So the GEnx counts as a running project, and any single launch carries the $2B.
S2 equals S1: a 10-year fps launched in 2050 enters service in 2060, after the last counted NB year (2056). S3's -0.08 is Embraer's jet entering in 2054 on the rival engine. Ghai and Ali both confirm these readings.

3. MY TESTS
- No birthright [CX-0564]: I read S2 and S3 as hard as S1. S2 costs $0 against S1 and S3 costs $0.08B, and hold is best in both.
- Additive and paid for the risk [CX-0301, CX-0355]: nothing is. The Ducted's S1 cost is its whole $5.78B gap; the best Open Fan plan loses at least $14.86B.
- Low case first [CX-0248, CX-0536]: S1 is the expected column on the record. Boeing: 'the business case isn't there yet' and 'you'll get a date from me when we launch'. Embraer: 'the numbers do not prove the return' and 'no decision to announce'. Booked at -10.0, not S1's -9.47.
- H2, the airframer sets the date [CX-0205, CX-0469]: an Open Fan ready in 2060 against NGSA's 2037 entry waits in every column. The RISE exception fails both parts: there is a penalty in every column, and the best plan needs $15.10B, above the $15B cap.
- H3, Ducted only as a defence: the trigger is on the record (GTF2 fitted next to CFM on NGSA; the Joint Venture commitment standing). I invoke it for the record only. It permits a defence; it does not pay for one. No column shows the Ducted buying back a slot. Ali adds that one year of slip takes its $0.22B to zero.
- Suppliers: hold adds no project and no strain. Ali reads the $2B as a floor, and supplier output is still unmeasured.
- Next generation, my 20% line [CX-0217, CX-0208]: no Ducted is in the orders, so the line is not engaged. The statement never calls a Ducted the next generation. RISE is the next engine, at a 'more than 20%' design point that is untested in flight (Ali).
- Tie-break: not needed. Hold leads every row by at least $5.58B, more than the $1B ε.
- Premium cap (H9): $0 this round. The game closes at $0.65B of $4.0B. The RISE allowance is unused.

4. TEAM RULE: I propose and decide
- Ghai's binding tests (pays for itself, volumes first, terms) all pass on hold. His binding vetoes cover every launch and are not engaged.
- Ali's binding date test passes: hold rests on no ready year. He now carries a binding veto on any Partner Embraer launch: its S3 +0.20 rests on CFM engines on Embraer's jet from 2054, before any new CFM engine is ready. I accept his tracing, and Ghai's reading of the +0.20 matches it. Hold does not engage it.
- Neither colleague's test fails on the plan I chose, so overrides is empty.

5. SAFRAN GATE (H7; CFM parity rule)
- ducted: hold, so consent is not engaged. Consent would have been assumed on the H3 trigger, but the order fails on money.
- open_fan: hold, so it is not engaged. A RISE product launch with no airframer path is outside joint practice, and there is no stated reason Safran would agree.
- partner_embraer: hold, so it is not engaged. It would follow consent on a passing CFM engine, and none passes.
- lobby_emissions: hold, so it is not engaged. It serves RISE and falls with the Open Fan.
- genx: GE alone, no gate.
Every NGSA, MAX, fps or Embraer supply or engine-talk move says price and capacity are joint with Safran [CX-0184, CX-0166, CX-0160]. Nothing is said on the partnership's term or renewal.

6. ALI'S READY YEARS AGAINST THE FIRST NEW-NB ENTRY (board years, not test results)
- Ducted 2056: 19 years after NGSA's 2037 entry, 2 years after the S3 Embraer jet (2054), 4 years ahead of the S2 fps (2060).
- Open Fan 2060: 23 years after NGSA and 6 years after the S3 jet.
- Partner Embraer counts from 2057.
- GEnx has been ready since 2033 and counting since 2042.
Flags and fleet data:
- No safety or durability flag is open on the LEAP family on NGSA or the MAX, or on GEnx, so I have nothing to answer cross-functionally this round [CX-0012].
- The LEAP-1B fleet outcome is not in Ali's record, so we claim nothing either way.
- Supplier output at the 9 suppliers and 15 sites is unmeasured.

7. RED LINES HELD
- H1: a LEAP derivative is on offer to every airframer.
- H2: no Open Fan wait.
- H3: no Ducted.
- H5: RISE is not cancelled and pays no programme dividend.
- H6: no date in the statement (Ali's watch list checked: no Ducted, Open Fan or RISE date, no CFM on Embraer's jet, no -1B result, no -1A figure beyond 'certified, in every new -1A engine, going in at shop visits').
- H7: Safran gate as above.
- H8: no rival or Joint Venture named, no blame.
- H9: $0 premium.
- My 20% and durability lines: not traded.

8. DOCTRINE, NOT MY RECORD, DROVE
- Partner Embraer and Lobby: doctrine §6, with my 'additive' rule applied.
- The Joint Venture response: doctrine §5 and §7, no public reaction and no price cut [CX-0609].
- Supply: Ali's memo, checked against doctrine (§2 strain as a floor; lean before capital).
- The LEAP-1B step-down move rests on Ali's CX-0010 and my deference to the airframer on rates [CX-0452]. Neither record covers the workforce, so we claim nothing on it.

9. BIASES, CHECKED
- Guide low and raise [CX-0270, CX-0654]: booking -10.0, up one step from round 3's -11.0 because the rivals held, but not to -9.47 while a Joint Venture can form.
- Installed-base lens ('the price of admission' [CX-0557]): it could rationalise a Ducted to be 'on' the fps. The fps is off the board, and CFM is always available on a new airframe.
- Deference to airframers: here the board's calendar closes the door, not deference.

10. WHAT HOLD GIVES UP
Nothing on the grid. Off the grid, a P&W-RR Joint Venture formed this round could cost about $2.0B and put the 2050 share at 49.9-50.1% (Ghai). No lever on this board acts on 2050. We answer it with time on wing, delivery and standard terms, jointly with Safran.

recommendations.text: Miss a cycle does not apply this round. `launch_if_selected` is not on the menu, because GTF2 has been ready since 2036. The ready GTF2 already covers every airframe still possible: an Embraer narrowbody launched in 2050 (EIS 2054, on P&W engines) and an fps on code 7 (EIS 2057 on the 7-year ramp, 2060 on the 10-year ramp or via Embraer). Hold both fields. A round of all holds does not come to review, and this is the last round, so these recommendations are the Board's closing record.

Bring the final annual GTF2 NPV review through the Finance Committee. Against Do Nothing, hold is worth +6.10 (engine +8.10, R&D -2.00). On the Board's reading of the brief's rounded table at 10%, about +5.3 of that was earned to 2049 and about +2.8 is still ahead. Against a buyback it is worth about +6.10. Record the commit's item value (-3.31 / -3.31 / -3.28) and its weighted value on Mitchill's weights and on Calio's `predictions`. Note that it gives up more than all the gain still ahead. The baseline tracked the plan: 1,299 engines in 2045 and 1,449 in 2049. The engine value gap over the status quo is +4.7 in 2050 (14.4 against 9.7), +5.8 at the 2052 peak and +4.9 in 2056. Use management's own figures, and invent none.

Joint Venture: hold, and open no terms. Answer Rolls-Royce's standing commitment publicly and respectfully: no Joint Venture to announce, and we share risk and investment with partners but never our core technology. Record internally that the 2045 revisit conditions are not met on this grid. The weighted item value is below zero, every column is below -$2B, and no live airframe carries code 1, 4, 5 or 7. With Rolls-Royce committed, a P&W commitment would form the Joint Venture at once. Rolls-Royce says it has 'no solo narrowbody programme', so a fold-in of our ready GTF2 is its route onto NGSA. That fold-in is the -3.31 the grid shows. Airbus leaves the question of whether Rolls-Royce counts as a third maker on NGSA to the game master. The grid's number decides, and the Board books no reading of that ruling.

Durability in the fleet. Bring GTF2's thirteen-year record on NGSA to the Governance and Public Policy Committee: time on wing, unscheduled removals, life-limited parts against full life, and the severe-environment fleet. Bring the GTF Hot Section kit's measured time on wing with it. State whether the CMC hot-section block deferred in 2035 is now proven. Until it is, it stays out of the fleet. The absence of a reported problem is not proof. No testing is compressed for any airframer's rate.

Capacity to the peak, with the fleet first. Confirm that tranche 2 to the 1,597 engine peak in 2052 is ordered, in steps against Airbus's rate-gated signals. Airbus has extended those signals to 2050 and sized them to its own needs. After the peak the hold row falls to 1,462 (2053), 1,351 (2056) and 951 (2060). Add no fixed plant, and plan how supplier and partner capacity is released after 2052. A possible Embraer line (S3, EIS 2054) ramps to 8 aircraft a month by 2060, about 192 engines a year at full rate. It fits inside that post-peak fall. Release capital for it only once a launch is on the record. The fleet keeps first call on constrained material.

Other moves toward the airframers. Keep GTF2 on offer, on standard terms, for any fps or new narrowbody that selects P&W, sole or shared. Boeing has restated that it will ask for code 7 at launch, with more than one engine source and durability first, and GTF2 is ready for that. Offer Embraer GTF2 or the GTF family at the Advantage standard, the choice being Embraer's. Claim no selection beyond NGSA, give no airframer's dates, and offer no discount, concession or free upgrade. A rival's discount never moves the answer.

Disclosure. The statement may say that GTF2 has been in service on NGSA since 2037, alongside CFM, because that is on the public record. It should cite time on wing only as measured fleet data and claim no durability the fleet has not shown. It should promise nothing on Airbus's, Boeing's or Embraer's dates or rates, claim no selection beyond NGSA's code 7, and announce no Joint Venture. Phrase durability as a record kept, not a claim, and give no ramp, peak or volume figure of ours.

Capital and the long view. Report the dividend, the pre-ASR debt path and the envelope fit for the round. Two holds add no new R&D, so GTF2's fleet cash goes to the dividend first, then debt, then buybacks as the fill-in. The Board's one-time stretch stays unused. The board's count ends in 2056, but the company's does not. Keep next-generation geared technology funded inside the roughly $6B self-funded envelope, as technology only, with no product, date or new bill. Bring its scope to the Finance Committee ranked by payback. As in 2016, the Board supplies the view beyond the three-year pay window. This recommendation is the Board's inference and has no grid effect.

frame.question:
Control what you can control [PX-0020]. Round 4, decision year 2050. This is the last round.

The engine work is done, and the plan held:
- The 2030 conditional order fired on NGSA's code 7.
- GTF2 has been ready since 2036 and in service on NGSA since 2037, fitted alongside CFM.
- Both objectives are met.

One of our two order fields is live:
- `gtf2_solo` has one legal value, `hold`. GTF2 is ready, so there is nothing to launch and nothing to cancel.
- `jv_with_rr` is the live question. Rolls-Royce has been committed since 2035, so a P&W `commit` is not an option we keep open. It forms the Joint Venture this round, folds our ready GTF2 (gear and core included) into a shared programme, and gives Rolls-Royce an equal narrowbody share through our engine. The grid prices it at -3.31 / -3.31 / -3.28 against `hold`. That is more than all of GTF2's remaining gain over Do Nothing on the board's count (about +2.74 in 2050-56).

I am asking four things:
1. Does anything on the grid, or anything we can prove, justify forming the Joint Venture in the last round? I expect not. Unlike 2045, the commit row (+2.79 / +2.79 / +2.88) keeps Capitalise met, so this round it is the grid and the gear that say no, not the objective.

4. How do we close in public? No durability the fleet has not shown, nothing on any airframer's dates or rates, no selection beyond NGSA, no Joint Venture.

The job has not changed. Set the safety and durability constraint, take the best PV inside it, and keep the gear ours.
frame.situation:
PUBLIC RECORD, 2050
- Airbus: NGSA launched 2030 and in service since 2037. Code 7 is final. CFM and P&W are fitted; Rolls-Royce was dropped because it was not ready by EIS. Airbus has extended its rate-gated signals to 2050, for NGSA engine sets only and sized to its own needs. It offers no payment and no take-or-pay. It "neither invites nor discourages" the Joint Venture. On its plain reading, fitting was settled at EIS and the Joint Venture would count as one source. Whether Rolls-Royce would then count as a third maker is left to the game master.
- P&W: GTF2 (Solo) launched 2030, ready since 2036.
- Rolls-Royce: `jv_with_pw: commit` has stood since 2035 and is restated "on standard terms, terms that credit the technology we bring". It has "No solo narrowbody programme". UltraFan stays technology inside base R&D. So folding in our GTF2 is its only route onto NGSA.
- Boeing: no fps launch. "I'm not going to pretend that waiting is free", but "the business case isn't there yet", and no date. At launch it will ask for code 7, with more than one engine source and durability first. The MAX is in its phase-out, and Boeing's share of narrowbody deliveries is down to 23.7% (2049).
- Embraer: "the numbers do not prove the return", no decision. It has logged readiness advice: 192 P&W engines a year behind Airbus's agreements, and a four-year clean-sheet certification. A narrowbody launched now would enter service in 2054 on P&W engines.
- CFM/GE: LEAP on NGSA. A LEAP derivative is on offer to every airframer. RISE stays technology, with no dates.
- Observed: P&W's share of narrowbody engines delivered rose from 24.2% (2026) to 41.7% (2049).

OUR POSITION (brief, hold/hold)
- ΔPV +6.10 $B: engine value +8.10, R&D -2.00. Yield 105.5%. GTF2's development spend is complete.
- The baseline tracked the plan: 1,299 engines delivered in 2045 and 1,449 in 2049, exactly tranche 1's target.
- Volumes ahead: 1,429 (2050), 1,548 (2051), the 1,597 peak (2052), then 1,462 (2053), 1,351 (2056, the last counted year) and 951 (2060). That is 40% below the peak.
- Engine value over the status quo: +4.7 in 2050 (14.4 against 9.7), +5.8 in 2052 and +4.9 in 2056.
- My reading of the brief's rounded table at 10%: about +5.31 of the gain over Do Nothing was earned to 2049, and about +2.74 is still ahead in 2050-56. The Board reads +5.3 and +2.8. Neil to confirm.

GRID (S1 rivals hold | S2 Boeing fps on the 10-year ramp, code 7 | S3 Embraer launches its narrowbody)
- Hold: +6.10 / +6.10 / +6.16. Best in every column.
- Hold + commit: +2.79 / +2.79 / +2.88.
- Item value of the commit: -3.31 / -3.31 / -3.28, which is 1.66x / 1.66x / 1.64x its own $2B bill.
- S2 equals S1. A 2050 fps enters service in 2060 on the 10-year ramp, or in 2057 on the 7-year ramp, both after the board stops counting narrowbody engines in 2056.
- S3 adds +0.06: an Embraer narrowbody entering service in 2054 on P&W engines.
- No column has a new narrowbody entering service without P&W.

OBJECTIVE STATUS
- Restore credibility: MET in all three columns. GTF2 has been in service on NGSA since 2037.
- Capitalise (ΔPV ≥ 0): MET under hold in all three. It would also stay met under the commit, but at $3.3B less.

BOARD (risk appetite 3.5, unchanged)
- Expects hold/hold, which is not a Board item, and asks for the full case as the closing record.
- Would veto a commit on four grounds: return hurdle, bounded downside, Joint Venture conditions, declared premium. It adds a fifth if the case rests on off-grid readings (Rolls-Royce as a third maker, an fps on code 1 or 4, value after 2056).
- Would also veto any item carrying an unresolved veto, a red-line flag or an override.

WHY NO JOINT VENTURE
- With Rolls-Royce committed, our `commit` is the formation, not an option. It is also final: there is no later round.
- It costs 1.64-1.66x its own bill in every column, about $3.3B. That is more than all the gain GTF2 still has ahead on the board's count.
- It hands an equal narrowbody share, and our gear and core, to a partner whose only route onto NGSA is our engine.
- Capitalise would stay met this time, so the grid and the red line decide, not the objective.
- My record on a Joint Venture is Low. This follows doctrine plus Neil's cash test and Shane's technical test.
- The partner relationship stays respectful [PX-0038].

TESTS
- Safety and durability: the fleet record is the test, and I want Shane's data.
- Visible demand: met on NGSA.
- Miss a cycle: no column has a new narrowbody entering service without P&W, and S2 equals S1 because of the board's 2056 count, not because we lose position. The cycle after GTF2 is answered by technology funding inside the envelope, not a launch. The rule is RTX-wide and applied to engines by inference [PX-0071].
- Dividend: no new R&D.
- Value, not share: standard terms throughout.

OTHER MOVES
Public:
1. GTF2 on offer on standard terms to any fps or new narrowbody that selects P&W, sole or shared. For Embraer, GTF2 or the GTF family at the Advantage standard, at Embraer's choice.
2. NGSA rate-gated supply agreements continue on standard terms.
3. A respectful answer to Rolls-Royce: no Joint Venture, no terms opened.
4. The Hot Section kit continues at shop visit; upgrades are sold, not given.
5. Next-generation geared technology funded as technology only.
Internal (the closing record):
1. The final GTF2 NPV review to the Finance Committee.
2. The fleet record and CMC status to the Governance and Public Policy Committee.
3. Tranche 2 to the peak, and the post-peak release plan, with the fleet first.
4. A record that the Joint Venture revisit conditions are not met.
5. The scope of technology work, ranked by payback.

PROPOSED DISCLOSURE, IN MY VOICE
"I'll start where we always start, with the fleet. For years the GTF fleet was not where it needed to be, and our customers carried that. We own it, and we have not forgotten it. So we control what we can control.

GTF2 has been in service on Airbus's next-generation single-aisle since 2037, alongside CFM. We judge it the way our customers do, on time on wing, and we report that record as the fleet measures it, not before. Any later-block feature enters the fleet only when it is proven and instrumented. We will not compress testing to meet anyone's rate.

Supply is where we have let customers down before. So we size castings and forgings capacity in steps, with our suppliers, against our customers' signals, and the fleet flying today keeps first call on material.

For any airframer that selects Pratt & Whitney, sole or shared, GTF2 is available today on standard terms. We're not in the early entry phase, the launch phase. The GTF Hot Section kit remains available at shop visit, on the same terms.

Rolls-Royce's commitment stands, and we respect it. We have no Joint Venture to announce. We share risk and investment with partners, never our core technology.

We keep investing in geared technology for the next cycle. It is technology, and we have no product or date to announce. If you miss a cycle in this business, you get shut out for decades, and we do not intend to miss one.

We speak for our engines, not for any airframer's dates or rates. We have learned our lesson from the prior iterations of the GTF. These are responsible bets with responsible paybacks."

cfo.memo:
Low end first. Hold/hold is +6.10 in our worst columns, rivals hold or a Boeing fps, and +6.16 if Embraer launches. On my weights, 0.50 / 0.35 / 0.15, unchanged because nobody's record changed, that's +6.11 expected. I book +6.10. A 2050 fps enters service in 2057 at the earliest, after the board stops counting, so S2 equals S1. That's timing, not position.

The Joint Venture costs 3.31 if nobody new selects it, and never less than 3.28: 1.64 to 1.66 times its own $2B bill. It's all share. Our $2B is spent and exactly fills our share, so there's no write-off and no new cash. It's the same split as 2045 over seven counted years instead of twelve. It gives back more than the 2.74 still ahead and leaves 2050-56 about $0.57B below Do Nothing. Any case for it rests on upside nobody has recorded. Ground 4, binding.

The review: 5.31 earned to 2049 and 2.74 ahead, on the rounded table. 1,299 and 1,449 delivered, exactly the 2045 forecast.

Cash: no new R&D, no cancel round, nothing at risk. The dividend and the debt path don't move. I have no 2050 debt figure, so I book no easing. Technology funding passes inside the envelope, and there's no number until the scope is known. "We do not intend to miss one" is intent, not a product. It clears.

The line falls 40% from the peak by 2060. That's demand, not share. Release the supplier tranches first.

ops.proposal:
PROPOSED ENGINE ORDERS (round 4, decision year 2050, the last round): gtf2_solo: hold; jv_with_rr: hold. Neither order is a Board item.

(1) PROPOSAL
gtf2_solo: hold
- It is the only legal value. GTF2 launched in 2030, has been ready since 2036, and has flown on NGSA since 2037 (code 7, fitted CFM + P&W).
- Hold keeps GTF2 on NGSA and ready for every EIS still possible.
- Grid row 'GTF2: hold' is +6.10 / +6.10 / +6.16, the best row in every column.
- Cancel is not legal, so I have no cancel test to flag.

jv_with_rr: hold
- Rolls-Royce has been committed since 2035, so a P&W commit is the formation itself, and it is final.
- No live airframe not yet in service carries code 1, 4, 5 or 7. NGSA is in service and its code is final.
- Readiness passes, but the gear condition fails: formation folds GTF2's gear and core into a shared programme on equal narrowbody shares [P-1233].
- The item value is -3.31 / -3.31 / -3.28 ('hold + commit' minus 'hold').
- My technical conditions fail on the gear. The call is Calio's, and I propose hold.

(2) READINESS. GTF2 has been ready since 2036.
- Embraer narrowbody launched in 2050: EIS 2054, 18 years after GTF2's ready year.
- fps launched in 2050: EIS 2057 on the 7-year ramp (+21), or 2060 on the 10-year ramp or via Embraer (+24).
- Joint Venture formed now with GTF2 folded in: ready 2050 on my reading of 'earlier if a partner folds in a solo programme that is further along'. If an engine that is already ready earns no credit, it is ready in 2056 (formation + 6), which would miss Embraer's 2054. The board fits only ready engines, so no order puts it on an airframe early.
- What the Joint Venture would bring that GTF2 does not: nothing any EIS needs.
  - UltraFan is technology inside Rolls-Royce's base R&D, and Rolls-Royce has 'no solo narrowbody programme'.
  - GTF2's development spend is complete, so there is no development risk left to share.
  - Rolls-Royce offers 'support through our partners'. That is shops, and shops were never what bound us. They wait on parts, not capacity [PX-0124]. We already run a partner network [PX-0118].
- Embraer engine, my engineering lean (inference; the choice is Embraer's). I have changed from 2045: I now lean to GTF2, provided the measured GTF2 record clears the Governance and Public Policy Committee first.
  - The reason is timing. An Embraer line ramps over 2054-60, inside GTF2's post-peak fall. Hold row plus Embraer never goes above 1,443 after 2053.
  - The GTF Advantage OE line ended with the A320neo tail by 2047, and its material now feeds the A320neo GTF fleet's shop visits, which keep first call.
  - If the record does not clear, I lean to the GTF family at the Advantage standard.
  - Both are installations, not developments.

(3) FLEET RECORD. It is not in my evidence or the brief, and the board does not model durability. I do not have:
- time on wing;
- unscheduled removals;
- life-limited parts against full life;
- severe-environment fleet data;
- the Hot Section kit's measured time on wing. My evidence stops at the 2025 target of 90-95% of the Advantage durability gains, embodied at shop visit from 2026 [PX-0088, PX-0106];
- CMC block status. I treat it as still waiting and out of the fleet. It enters only as a later block, instrumented and proven at no less than the Advantage endurance multiple [P-1214, P-1215, P-0779].
What the brief does show:
- 14,579 P&W narrowbody engines delivered in 2037-49, with GTF2 and the GTF tail not split. The tail ended by 2047, so the 2048-49 engines (2,838) are all GTF2.
- No AOG, escape or removal figure on the record.
That is the absence of a reported problem, not proof [PX-0112]. At those volumes the fleet is far past the 1M-hour maturity benchmark [P-0847] (inference). So the record exists inside the company; it just is not here. The statement gets no figure.

(4) CAPACITY. Numbers are the hold row; the arithmetic is mine.
Tranche 2 status:
- The 2045 decision ordered tranche 2 (+148 over 1,449, to 1,597 in 2052) 'by about 2049'.
- My advice to release the 2051 step (+99) in 2048 was in my veto note. Neither the brief nor the ExCo notes record whether it went, and the board does not model parts. I cannot confirm it from the record, and I will not claim it.
- The brief shows tranche 1 landed: 1,449 in 2049, exactly the target.
- Any tranche 2 balance still open goes this year. At 2-2.5 years of forging lead [P-0079], an order placed now lands in 2052 to mid-2052, the late edge.
- If the 2051 step slipped, 2051 is paced to parts and the fleet keeps first call.
New point:
- Airbus's rate-gated signals run only to 2050, at about 54-59 P&W sets a month, which is 1,296-1,416 engines a year.
- In engines a year, the row runs 1,449 (2049, about 60.4 sets a month), 1,429 (2050, 59.5), 1,548 (2051, 64.5) and 1,597 (2052, 66.5).
- So the peak step is 132-181 engines a year above Airbus's signalled band, and beyond its horizon. It stays supplier and partner capacity only, with step-down rights, and we ask Airbus for 2051-52 signals.
Way down:
- Step 1, 2053. Release the peak step, 1,597 to 1,462 (-135, -8.5%). That is most of tranche 2.
- Step 2, 2054-56. Release tranche 1's +88 above the 2044 base of 1,361 as the row falls: 1,443 (+82), 1,396 (+35), 1,351 (-10).
  - If Embraer is on the record (S3), keep tranche 1 suppliers through 2056. Hold plus Embraer is 1,428 in 2055 and 1,415 in 2056, against 1,449.
- Step 3, 2057-60. The row runs below the 2044 base: 1,220 (-141), 1,101 (-260), 1,024 (-337), 951 (-410; -40.5% from the peak).
  - No fixed plant was added after 2044, so nothing new is stranded.
  - The freed base swings to castings and forgings for the installed GTF and GTF2 fleet's shop visits first: LLP replacements and Hot Section kits.
  - Then it goes to any Embraer line: about 96 gross engines in 2057, rising to 192 in 2060. Hold plus Embraer is 1,143 in 2060, still 218 under the base.
  - The board does not model MRO, so I put no number on shop-visit demand. The shops' measured parts demand gets first call [PX-0123, PX-0099, PX-0110].
Retention rule, now that the game ends without a Boeing answer. Keep a supplier only against one of these:
- the installed fleet's shop-visit parts demand;
- Airbus's rate-gated signal;
- a launch on the public record whose need falls inside lead time.
Because a 2050 fps enters service in 2057 or 2060 and Embraer in 2054, both are well beyond the 2-2.5-year lead. So I pre-qualify suppliers with no capital, and buy capacity only once a launch is on the record.

(5) ENGINEERING LOAD. There is no strain charge on this board; this is my judgement.
- None of it is a new engine development:
  - CMC block: run to test results, not a date;
  - Hot Section embodiment: sustaining work;
  - Embraer installation: 2050-54, if launched;
  - fps installation: 2050-57 or 2050-60, if launched;
  - next-generation geared work: technology only.
- The 2045 order holds when work collides: fleet, then an installation with a date on the record, then the CMC block, then technology.
- We can carry it all if fleet engineering stays ring-fenced with first call. The stretch case is Embraer 2054 plus an fps on the 7-year ramp to 2057, both installations of a ready engine.
- I have no headcount data.
On the cycle after GTF2: extend the GTF [PX-0129 inference]. The technology list on our record is composite fan blades, CMC hot-section parts and a next-generation fan-drive gear [P-0790]. The CMC later block is where hot-section technology gets proven in the fleet first, instrumented [P-1214]. The GTF2 fleet record is the data base for the next gear, so keep it ours.

(6) JOINT VENTURE, TECHNICAL. Formation puts GTF2's gear and core into a shared programme on equal narrowbody shares, so I raise the gear flag. The 2045 revisit conditions are not met on this grid:
- weighted item value below 0 (-3.31 / -3.31 / -3.28): fails;
- no column below -$2B: fails in all three;
- Rolls-Royce committed: met;
- ready by EIS: passes with the fold-in;
- gear-and-core terms (P&W owns the gear and core modules and their data, holds the type certificate and continued airworthiness, and licenses IP for the Joint Venture product only): not met. Rolls-Royce's terms 'credit the technology we bring', and the board gives equal shares.

(7) VETO CHECKS
- Row A passes both of my grounds.
- Row B: no binding veto, since readiness passes and nothing is launched. The gear flag stands as a company red line.
- Calio's draft statement passes both grounds:
  - no time-on-wing or durability figure, and durability is a record we report;
  - 'since 2037, alongside CFM' is on the public record;
  - no ramp, peak or volume figure, and no airframer's date or rate.
- Advice: keep 'not in the early entry phase' next to 'standard terms', so it reads as pricing [PX-0055]. 'We do not intend to miss one' is intent, with no product or date, and passes my grounds; ground 4 is Mitchill's call.
- The parts view is my own record. The Joint Venture, Embraer, load and MRO views are the seat's doctrine or inference.
- I checked the PV split on the brief's rounded rows at 10%: +5.31 to 2049 and +2.74 in 2050-56. The commit gives up 0.57 more than all the gain still ahead.

ops.would_change_mind_if:
The order fields are settled. Hold is legal and dominant, and this is the last round. What would change is the operating plan.

- Measured GTF2 fleet data shows a shortfall: removals above plan, LLPs short of full life, or severe-environment time on wing short.
  - I contain first with a dated recovery, and the fleet takes first call.
  - The NGSA rate is paced to parts, and my Embraer lean goes back to the GTF family at the Advantage standard.
- The data comes in clean.
  - A measured time-on-wing figure can go in the statement.
  - GTF2 becomes my lead offer to Embraer.
- CMC test results come in proven and instrumented. Then the CMCs enter as a later block. Not before.
- Airbus signals 2051-52 below our tranche 2. Then the peak step is released early, to the fleet's shop visits.
- An Embraer or fps launch goes on the record. Then I keep tranche 1 suppliers through 2056 and release the pre-qualified capacity. The capacity plan changes, not these orders.
- On the Joint Venture, nothing on this grid. I would need all of these:
  - an item value of 0 or more, with no column below -$2B;
  - the engine ready by EIS;
  - terms keeping P&W's gear and core modules, data and type certificate ours.
ops.memo:
The bad number first. GTF2 has been on NGSA for thirteen years, and we delivered 14,579 P&W narrowbody engines in 2037-49. I still can't give the Governance and Public Policy Committee a measured GTF2 record. I have no time on wing, removal rate, LLP count, severe-environment data, Hot Section figure or CMC result, and neither does the brief. No reported problem is not proof. I said "no surprise coming" once, and I won't say it again. So no figure goes in the statement, and the CMC block stays out of the fleet.

My proposal: `gtf2_solo: hold`, `jv_with_rr: hold`. GTF2 has been ready since 2036 and beats every EIS left: Embraer 2054 (+18 years) and an fps in 2057 or 2060 (+21, +24). Hold is best in every column: +6.10 / +6.10 / +6.16.

The Joint Venture adds shops, and shops were never our constraint. Parts were. Formation puts our gear and core into a shared programme, so I raise the gear flag. That's the company's red line, not one of my veto grounds.

Capacity: 1,429 engines this year, the 1,597 peak in 2052, then down 40% to 951 by 2060. Airbus's signals run only to 2050 and top out near 1,416 of ours, so the peak step stays supplier capacity and comes off from 2053. From 2056, freed material goes to the fleet's shop visits first.

Both my checks pass. My record is one investor day, June 2023. The Joint Venture, Embraer and capacity views are the seat's doctrine.

decision.public_statement:
I'll start where we always start, with the fleet. For years the GTF fleet was not where it needed to be, and our customers carried that. We own it, and we have not forgotten it. So we control what we can control.

GTF2 has been in service on Airbus's next-generation single-aisle since 2037, alongside CFM. We judge it the way our customers do, on time on wing. We will report that record as the fleet measures it, and not before. Any later-block feature enters the fleet only when it is proven and instrumented. We will not compress testing to meet anyone's rate.

Supply is where we have let customers down before. So we size castings and forgings capacity in steps, with our suppliers, against our customers' signals, and the fleet flying today keeps first call on material.

For any airframer that selects Pratt & Whitney, sole or shared, GTF2 is ready today, on standard terms. We're not in the early entry phase, the launch phase. The GTF Hot Section kit remains available at shop visit, on the same standard terms.

Rolls-Royce's commitment stands, and we respect it. We have no Joint Venture to announce. We share risk and investment with partners, never our core technology.

We keep investing in geared technology for the next cycle, inside the R&D we already fund. It is technology, and we have no product or date to announce. If you miss a cycle in this business, you get shut out for decades, and we do not intend to miss one.

We speak for our engines, not for any airframer's dates or rates. We have learned our lesson from the prior iterations of the GTF. These are responsible bets with responsible paybacks.
decision.rationale:
DECISION: `gtf2_solo: hold`, `jv_with_rr: hold`. Premium $0B. `overrides` empty. Neither order is a Board item. This is the last round, so this note is the closing record: all the data, with all the thinking [PG-0016].

TEAM RULE, STEP BY STEP
1. Start from Eddy's proposal: hold / hold.
2. Strike plans that fail a binding veto.
   - Mitchill's ground 4 (booking upside before it is proven) binds against `jv_with_rr: commit`. The commit has no gain column (-3.31 / -3.31 / -3.28), so any case for it would rest on something not on the record: a third-maker ruling for Rolls-Royce on NGSA, an fps on code 1 or 4, value after 2056, partner money toward a bill already paid, or a Rolls-Royce withdrawal. Row B is struck.
   - Eddy raised no binding veto on either row, and Row A passes all six grounds.
   - Eddy's gear flag on Row B is a company red line [P-1233]. I confirm it, and holding the field strikes it. Red lines are never traded for PV.
3. Safety and durability constraint first [PX-0035, PX-0073]. GTF2 was ready in 2036, ahead of every EIS still possible: Embraer 2054 (+18 years) and an fps in 2057 on the 7-year ramp or 2060 on the 10-year ramp or via Embraer (+21, +24). The fleet record is now the durability test. Eddy says plainly that he cannot yet bring a measured record, and I take that as a gap, not as proof [PX-0112]. So the statement carries no figure, the CMC block stays out of the fleet, and the record goes to the Governance and Public Policy Committee as a dated follow-up.
4. Optimise inside the constraint. Hold is the best row in every column: +6.10 / +6.10 / +6.16 against +2.79 / +2.79 / +2.88. The ranking holds on any weights.

THE GRID AND THE WEIGHTS
I take Mitchill's weights, 0.50 / 0.35 / 0.15, over my framing weights of 0.45 / 0.35 / 0.20.
- We agree on S2.
- S3 is the only column above S1. 'Book on the record' argues for his 0.15, and I trust his numbers over my own dates.

| Weights | Hold | Commit | Item value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mitchill's | +6.11 | +2.80 | -3.31 (-3.3055) |
| Mine | +6.11 | +2.81 | -3.30 |
| Equal | +6.12 | +2.82 | -3.30 |

- Booked number: +6.10 (S1, on the record).
- The commit's loss is 1.66x / 1.66x / 1.64x its own $2B bill.
- It gives up about $0.57B more than the +2.74 still ahead in 2050-56, which would leave those years below Do Nothing.
- The cost is all share: $0 write-off and $0 new spend, with the same equal split as 2045 over 7 counted years instead of 12 (6.69 x 8.52 / 17.25 = 3.30).
- S2 equals S1 because of timing, not position: a 2050 fps enters service after the 2056 count.
- No column has a new narrowbody entering service without P&W.

MY TESTS
- Safety and durability: pass.
- Visible demand: met on NGSA's code 7, which is on the record. `launch` and `launch_if_selected` are off the menu.
- Miss a cycle: no column has a new narrowbody without P&W. The cycle after GTF2 is answered by technology funding inside the envelope, not a launch. The rule is RTX-wide and applied to engines by inference [PX-0071].
- Responsible bet: the doctrine order, the best-PV order and the objective order are the same, so the premium is $0.
- Dividend: $0 of new R&D. The dividend and the pre-ASR debt path are untouched, the envelope fits, and the stretch stays unused. Mitchill confirms. The brief has no 2050 debt figure, so no easing is booked.
- Value, not share: standard terms throughout, with no concession [PX-0055, PX-0100].
- Objective status: both objectives met in every column, and $0 of PV given up.

SHARED-SOURCE RELIEF
GTF2 rides code 7 alongside CFM, against the sole-source red line [P-0746]. I declare the relief at $0B as franchise defence [PX-0058, P-1292].

DOCTRINE, NOT MY RECORD
My record on a Joint Venture is Low. That answer follows doctrine [P-1233, P-1875], Mitchill's cash test and Eddy's technical test.

BIASES NAMED
- Architecture loyalty [PX-0014] points the same way as the grid. It is not the reason.
- My optimism on dates [PX-0017, PX-0098] keeps every ramp, peak and volume figure out of the statement.
- Supply-first caution [PX-0085]: the peak step above Airbus's signals stays supplier capacity with step-down rights.
- My under-call of the 2030 launch [PX-0093] was why I lifted S2 in the frame. S2 does not move the answer.

CHANGES FROM THE FRAME
1. I take Mitchill's weights.
2. Mitchill's advice: 'inside the R&D we already fund' is added to the next-cycle sentence.
3. Eddy's advice: 'not in the early entry phase' stays next to 'standard terms'.
4. Eddy's retention rule replaces 2045's rule of holding suppliers until a Boeing fps resolves, because the game ends without that answer.
5. Any open tranche 2 balance is released this year, and Airbus is asked for 2051-52 signals.

None of these changes the grid.

final.public_statement:
I'll start where we always start, with the fleet. For years the GTF fleet was not where it needed to be, and our customers carried that. We own it, and we have not forgotten it. So we control what we can control.

GTF2 has been in service on Airbus's next-generation single-aisle since 2037, alongside CFM. We judge it the way our customers do, on time on wing. We will report that record as the fleet measures it, and not before. Any later-block feature enters the fleet only when it is proven and instrumented. We will not compress testing to meet anyone's rate.

Supply is where we have let customers down before. So we size castings and forgings capacity in steps, with our suppliers, against our customers' signals, and the fleet flying today keeps first call on material.

For any airframer that selects Pratt & Whitney, sole or shared, GTF2 is ready today, on standard terms. We're not in the early entry phase, the launch phase. The GTF Hot Section kit remains available at shop visit, on the same standard terms.

Rolls-Royce's commitment stands, and we respect it. We have no Joint Venture to announce. We share risk and investment with partners, never our core technology.

We keep investing in geared technology for the next cycle, inside the R&D we already fund. It is technology, and we have no product or date to announce. If you miss a cycle in this business, you get shut out for decades, and we do not intend to miss one.

We speak for our engines, not for any airframer's dates or rates. We have learned our lesson from the prior iterations of the GTF. These are responsible bets with responsible paybacks.
final.rationale:
DECISION: `gtf2_solo: hold`, `jv_with_rr: hold`. Premium $0B. `overrides` empty. Neither order is a Board item. This is the last round, so this note is the closing record: all the data, with all the thinking [PG-0016].

TEAM RULE, STEP BY STEP
1. Start from Eddy's proposal: hold / hold.
2. Strike plans that fail a binding veto.
   - Mitchill's ground 4 (booking upside before it is proven) binds against `jv_with_rr: commit`. The commit has no gain column (-3.31 / -3.31 / -3.28), so any case for it would rest on something not on the record: a third-maker ruling for Rolls-Royce on NGSA, an fps on code 1 or 4, value after 2056, partner money toward a bill already paid, or a Rolls-Royce withdrawal. Row B is struck.
   - Eddy raised no binding veto on either row, and Row A passes all six grounds.
   - Eddy's gear flag on Row B is a company red line [P-1233]. I confirm it, and holding the field strikes it. Red lines are never traded for PV.
3. Safety and durability constraint first [PX-0035, PX-0073]. GTF2 was ready in 2036, ahead of every EIS still possible: Embraer 2054 (+18 years) and an fps in 2057 on the 7-year ramp or 2060 on the 10-year ramp or via Embraer (+21, +24). The fleet record is now the durability test. Eddy says plainly that he cannot yet bring a measured record, and I take that as a gap, not as proof [PX-0112]. So the statement carries no figure, the CMC block stays out of the fleet, and the record goes to the Governance and Public Policy Committee as a dated follow-up.
4. Optimise inside the constraint. Hold is the best row in every column: +6.10 / +6.10 / +6.16 against +2.79 / +2.79 / +2.88. The ranking holds on any weights.

THE GRID AND THE WEIGHTS
I take Mitchill's weights, 0.50 / 0.35 / 0.15, over my framing weights of 0.45 / 0.35 / 0.20.
- We agree on S2.
- S3 is the only column above S1. 'Book on the record' argues for his 0.15, and I trust his numbers over my own dates.

|---|---|---|---|
| Mitchill's | +6.11 | +2.80 | -3.31 (-3.3055) |
| Mine | +6.11 | +2.81 | -3.30 |
| Equal | +6.12 | +2.82 | -3.30 |

- Booked number: +6.10 (S1, on the record).
- The commit's loss is 1.66x / 1.66x / 1.64x its own $2B bill.
- It gives up about $0.57B more than the +2.74 still ahead in 2050-56, which would leave those years below Do Nothing.
- The cost is all share: $0 write-off and $0 new spend, with the same equal split as 2045 over 7 counted years instead of 12 (6.69 x 8.52 / 17.25 = 3.30).
- S2 equals S1 because of timing, not position: a 2050 fps enters service after the 2056 count.
- No column has a new narrowbody entering service without P&W.

MY TESTS
- Safety and durability: pass.
- Visible demand: met on NGSA's code 7, which is on the record. `launch` and `launch_if_selected` are off the menu.
- Miss a cycle: no column has a new narrowbody without P&W. The cycle after GTF2 is answered by technology funding inside the envelope, not a launch. The rule is RTX-wide and applied to engines by inference [PX-0071].
- Responsible bet: the doctrine order, the best-PV order and the objective order are the same, so the premium is $0.
- Dividend: $0 of new R&D. The dividend and the pre-ASR debt path are untouched, the envelope fits, and the stretch stays unused. Mitchill confirms. The brief has no 2050 debt figure, so no easing is booked.
- Value, not share: standard terms throughout, with no concession [PX-0055, PX-0100].
- Objective status: both objectives met in every column, and $0 of PV given up.

SHARED-SOURCE RELIEF
GTF2 rides code 7 alongside CFM, against the sole-source red line [P-0746]. I declare the relief at $0B as franchise defence [PX-0058, P-1292].

DOCTRINE, NOT MY RECORD
My record on a Joint Venture is Low. That answer follows doctrine [P-1233, P-1875], Mitchill's cash test and Eddy's technical test.

BIASES NAMED
- Architecture loyalty [PX-0014] points the same way as the grid. It is not the reason.
- My optimism on dates [PX-0017, PX-0098] keeps every ramp, peak and volume figure out of the statement.
- Supply-first caution [PX-0085]: the peak step above Airbus's signals stays supplier capacity with step-down rights.
- My under-call of the 2030 launch [PX-0093] was why I lifted S2 in the frame. S2 does not move the answer.

CHANGES FROM THE FRAME
1. I take Mitchill's weights.
2. Mitchill's advice: 'inside the R&D we already fund' is added to the next-cycle sentence.
3. Eddy's advice: 'not in the early entry phase' stays next to 'standard terms'.
4. Eddy's retention rule replaces 2045's rule of holding suppliers until a Boeing fps resolves, because the game ends without that answer.
5. Any open tranche 2 balance is released this year, and Airbus is asked for 2051-52 signals.

It gives no airframer's dates or rates, claims no selection beyond NGSA, announces no Joint Venture, and gives no ramp, peak or volume figure. Mitchill cleared it on ground 4, and Eddy on ground 1.

board_response.recommendation: 8. Capital and the long view: dividend, pre-ASR debt path, envelope; next-generation geared technology funded inside the envelope, scope to the Finance Committee ranked by payback.
board_response.response:
Taken up.
- Two holds add $0 of new R&D. The dividend comes first, then debt back to pre-ASR levels, with buybacks as the fill-in.
- The envelope fits, and the one-time stretch stays unused.
- The brief has no 2050 debt figure, so no easing is booked. The 2030E broker anchors (0.76x and 0.94x) are context only.
- Technology-only geared work is a reallocation inside the roughly $6B envelope. Publicly there is no product, date or bill. Internally its scope goes to the Finance Committee ranked by payback.

board_review.note: No Board items: every order is the default.

priorities: 1. Product safety comes first: 'product safety, which is and always must be our most important priority'. No engine of ours enters service before it is ready. NGSA has flown CFM and P&W since 2037 and no fps is on the record, so no live airframe that is not yet in service carries an RR code. Our only narrowbody route is the standing Joint Venture commitment. If P&W commits this round (S3), the Joint Venture forms around GTF2, which has been ready since 2036 and flying on NGSA for thirteen years. The grid counts our share in 2050 itself (26.1%). Watson must therefore confirm three things: nothing is compressed, UltraFan content enters only as later insertions, and support is in place before our share starts. No dates in public [RG-0027, RG-0025, R-0970, R-1476, RX-0296, RX-0283, RX-0284].

2. Protect the widebody cash cow (Control's mission).
- Our own narrowbody money stays within $4B. The Joint Venture share is $4.0B and is spent only in S3. An UltraFan NB Solo in either form puts $8.0B at risk.
- Never a narrowbody and a widebody programme on record together. Beside the standing commitment, a Trent 1000 upgrade or UltraFan WB charges $5B of strain in S3.
- Widebody share is 55.2% in 2050 in every column with no programme (58.0% in S5), above the 50% line.
- On this grid every widebody programme is pure cost. The upgrade counts only from 2053, so 2050 share does not move. UltraFan WB has no Re-engine on the record to fly [RG-0068, R-1574, RX-0214, R-0929, R-1127].

3. Decide the 2050 review of the standing commitment on the 2050 grid, as agreed last round (our recommendation 7 and the ExCo's private 2050 test). Our lean is to keep it: `jv_with_pw: hold`.
- Row 'UltraFan NB: hold + withdraw JV commitment' against 'UltraFan NB: hold' is 0, 0, -1.22, 0, 0, 0. A withdraw gains nothing in any column and loses 1.22 if P&W commits.
- The formation column has shrunk, from +15.23 in 2035 and +6.57 in 2045 to +1.22 now, because the board counts narrowbody only to 2056. It is still above 0.
- Its off-grid worst case is the $4B bill and no worse.
When we commit something, we honor it [R-1010, RX-0124, R-0318, R-0916, RG-0033, R-1573].

4. Profit over share in the last round. Nothing after 2050 can rescue an item: narrowbody is counted to 2056 and widebody to 2061. The brief's own verdict is 'UltraFan NB: hold' as the best plan in every column. Item values on our illustrative weights:
- Solo: -7.20.
- `launch_if_selected`: -0.80, and -8.00 in S2.
- Upgrade beside the commitment: -2.22, worst -6.73.
- UltraFan WB: -4.43, worst -9.00.
- Withdraw: -0.12.
The enter-narrowbody objective can no longer be met in full, because 2045 was 0.0%. Only its 2050 half is still open, through S3, and we pay no premium for it [R-1011, R-1582, R-1561, RG-0033, R-1005].

5. The balance sheet and the capital order stand: balance sheet first, then the dividend (30-40%), then investment and extra distributions. In S3 our $4B share, about £2.94bn at 1.36 $/£, is funded from free cash flow and redeployed from base UltraFan maturation inside a broadly flat R&D envelope. No equity, no new borrowing, no borrowing for buybacks. No balance-sheet trigger is live [RX-0242, RG-0041, RG-0059, R-0900, RX-0214].
board_guidance.risk_appetite: Averse, 4 of 5, in the last round. We accept only the staged, shared risk already on the record: the standing Joint Venture commitment. It costs nothing unless P&W commits. If P&W does commit, it is worth +1.22 for $4.0B of our money, with no strain and a worst case of its own bill. We will not accept a new unconditional launch, a narrowbody item with a negative weighted value, an item that can lose more than its own bill, or a widebody programme beside a commitment that could form this round.

recommendations.text:
Keep the standing Joint Venture commitment: `jv_with_pw: hold`. This is the 2050 review we asked for last round, decided on the 2050 grid.
- If P&W commits, 'UltraFan NB: hold' is +0.66, against -0.56 for the withdraw row: +1.22 for $4.0B of our money, with no strain.
- A withdraw gains nothing in any column.
- The off-grid worst case is the bill, -4.00, and no worse. That case is the one Airbus has raised in public: fitting 'settled at EIS', and whether Rolls-Royce counts as a third maker is a ruling for the game master.
Read it openly in `rationale` against the ExCo's own 2050 test. This is not options management: an airframe can still use the engine, and the commitment costs nothing unless P&W comes. When we commit something, we honor it.

Safety first. Watson should rule on what a 2050 formation means.
- The ready year the board prices is the formation year: GTF2 has been ready since 2036 and in service on NGSA since 2037.
- Nothing is compressed.
- UltraFan content goes in only as later insertions, each on its own test programme, and the case counts on none of it.
- The support plan is in place before our share starts, which on the grid is 2050 itself. P&W's GTF2 network on NGSA is the base. Partner shops follow the Singapore model. Spares and field service sit inside the $4B. Castings and forgings come off the Trent lines.
He should report through the Safety, Energy Transition & Tech Committee. If he cannot confirm it, he should say so with his reasons, and the board will then accept a withdraw.

Hold UltraFan NB Solo in both forms.
- The unconditional launch has no airframe on the record. It would be ready in 2057, after the narrowbody market the board counts ends in 2056. It loses $8B in five columns.
- `launch_if_selected` fires only in S2, where an fps launched now enters service in 2060: -8.00, and $8.0B against Control's bound.
Boeing has said it will request code 7 at launch, not code 5. Airframers go first, and we won't do anything not profitable. Our narrowbody entry is the Joint Venture.

No widebody programme this round.
- Widebody share is 55.2% in 2050 in every column (58.0% in S5), above the 50% line, and no Re-engine is on the record.
- The upgrade counts only from 2053, so it buys nothing on our 2050 measures. Beside the standing commitment it is -2.22 weighted, worst -6.73. UltraFan WB is -4.43, worst -9.00. Both are worse than their own bills, and both would break 'never both' in S3.
- If the ExCo nevertheless wants the upgrade, bring it only beside a withdraw, with McCabe's co-signature and at least $1.72B declared in `premium_b`. Price openly what it gives up: -2.27 against -0.42 at plan level, and the commitment's +1.22 in S3. We would approve it but do not recommend it.
Protect the widebody core through Trent time on wing and durability inside base R&D.

Disclosure and terms in the final statement.
- No entry, ready or airframer date, and nothing on when our share would join NGSA's fleet. 'Maturity sets the date, and we compress nothing' is the right register.
- Do not comment on NGSA's fitting or on how Airbus counts its engine sources. That is their call, and the game master's ruling.
- Restate the standing commitment on standard terms, respectfully, with no payment or concession to induce P&W or Airbus. 'Terms that credit the technology we bring' asks for value; it is not a concession.
- Any change of terms comes back with joint CEO-CFO sign-off.

Capital.
- Show our Joint Venture share against a broadly flat R&D envelope: $4B, which is £2.94bn at 1.36 $/£. Booked at formation, it falls in one year, because the folded engine is ready at once, so redeploy it from base UltraFan maturation.
- The 2026 analyst models end in 2030-31, so any 2050 cash comparison is inference.
- The capital order stands: balance sheet, then the dividend, then investment. No equity, no new borrowing, no borrowing for buybacks.

Close the game on the record. This is the last round, so no review follows.
- State in `objective_note` that enter-narrowbody cannot now be met in full, because 2045 was 0.0%. Only its 2050 half remains open, through S3, and no PV is spent chasing it.
- State that widebody dominance and both of Control's mission measures are met in every column on the lean.
- The commitment then stands unformed at game end unless P&W commits, at no cost.

frame.question:
So. 2050 is the last round, and I want it framed in cash and quality of earnings. After this round nothing can earn back a new programme. The board counts narrowbody to 2056 and widebody to 2061. On this grid every new programme loses money in every column.

The live question is the 2050 review of the Joint Venture commitment we made in public in 2035. We set the test ourselves last round: keep it if the formation column is at least 0 against a withdraw and its off-grid worst case stays within the $4B bill.
- Keep it (`jv_with_pw: hold`). It costs nothing unless P&W commits. If P&W does commit (S3), it is worth +1.22 against a withdraw. That is down from +6.57 in 2045, because the counted market is now short.
- Or withdraw it. A withdraw gains nothing in any column.

Second question: is any widebody or Solo money worth spending when hold is the best plan in every column? I say no. I want both of you to test that, not take it from me.

Airframes (public record)
- NGSA (Airbus): launched 2030, in service since 2037. Code 7 is final. Fitted: CFM + P&W GTF2. RR was dropped because it was not ready by EIS.

Engines

- CFM/GE: the GEnx upgrade has been ready since 2033. It took our widebody share from 58.0% to 55.2% from 2042. A LEAP derivative is on offer to every airframer. RISE stays technology.

Widebody Re-engines: none on the record, A350 or 787.

Our position
- ΔPV -0.56 if nobody moves (yield 99.49%).
- Hold row weighted -0.42 (S1 0.55, S2 0.10, S3 0.10, S4 0.10, S5 0.05, S6 0.10).
- The brief's verdict: 'UltraFan NB: hold' is the best plan in every column.

Objectives
- Enter narrowbody: not met (0.0% in 2045 and 2050). It cannot be met in full, because 2045 is gone. Only the 2050 half is open, and only through S3 (26.1%).
- Widebody dominance: met. 55.2% in the worst year, 58.0% in S5.
- Control's mission: met. $0.0B of our own narrowbody money and $0 strain today.

Board guidance (non-binding; its veto comes after my decision)
- It leans to all-hold, with the commitment kept.
- It would veto:
  - a withdraw on its own on the present record;
  - a Solo in either form;
  - UltraFan WB in any plan;
  - the upgrade beside the commitment;
  - the upgrade beside a withdraw without McCabe's co-signature and at least $1.72B declared as premium.
- It would approve withdraw + upgrade but does not recommend it. It would accept a withdraw on its own only if Watson rules, with reasons, that a 2050 formation compresses maturity or cannot have support in place before our share starts.
